propositions: The gate matches field names globally as a set of bare strings, allowing a field to pass if any same-named attribute on any unrelated config is read anywhere in src/rebar, creating false negatives for inert fields whose names are reused.

CodeHealthConfig.enabled had zero read sites but passed the gate because .enabled is read on unrelated configs (UiConfig, McpConfig, EnsureConfig), while uniquely-named CodeHealthConfig.analyzers correctly tripped the gate.

The fix must resolve each attribute read to its owning dataclass through receiver analysis (section names, parameter annotations, local assignments, return types, and cross-module fixed-point binding) rather than matching bare terminal names.

Four newly-flagged fields are live and read through documented indirection (config.py plumbing, string-keyed access, or __post_init__ validation) and receive accurate # read-via: markers naming their actual readers.
Existing gate tests must migrate to the owner-resolution contract by making receivers resolvable through annotation, section name, or call-site binding, rather than loosening the resolver.
The gate must report any # read-via: marker whose pointer names a closed rebar ticket id, so expired exemptions surface instead of persisting silently.
